quick: 15 mg/kg/day IM (usually 1 g/day); max 1 g/day, less in elderly
Small amounts in milk; use with caution
Audiometry, vestibular function, renal function, levels
summary: Streptomycin is a parenteral (intramuscular) aminoglycoside antibiotic used mainly as part of combination therapy for tuberculosis and for selected serious infections such as plague, tularemia, brucellosis and enterococcal endocarditis. The usual adult dose is about 15 mg/kg/day (commonly 1 g/day) IM, with reductions for elderly and renal-impaired patients. It carries a BOXED WARNING for neurotoxicity, ototoxicity (potentially irreversible hearing/vestibular loss) and nephrotoxicity, mandating audiometric and renal monitoring. It is contraindicated in pregnancy.
indications: Tuberculosis (as part of a multidrug regimen)
Enterococcal endocarditis and streptococcal endocarditis (combined with penicillin/ampicillin)
Other serious gram-negative infections when susceptibility is documented and safer agents are unsuitable

dosage.d: 15 mg/kg/day IM (usually 1 g/day), or 25-30 mg/kg 2-3 times weekly in intermittent regimens
dosage.n: Max 1 g/day; reduce to <=750 mg/day in elderly; part of multidrug therapy

dosage.d: 1 g IM every 12 h for 2 weeks, then 500 mg every 12 h, with penicillin/ampicillin
dosage.n: Use only if high-level gentamicin resistance / per susceptibility

dosage.d: Reduce dose and/or extend dosing interval per renal function and levels
dosage.n: Guide by serum concentrations and CrCl

admin: Give by deep intramuscular injection into a large muscle (rotate sites)
Reconstitute per product instructions; not for routine IV push
Ensure adequate hydration to reduce nephrotoxicity
Always use as part of combination therapy for tuberculosis
Adjust dose using serum levels and renal function, especially with prolonged use
moa: Streptomycin binds irreversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit of susceptible bacteria, causing misreading of mRNA and inhibition of protein synthesis, which is bactericidal. Like other aminoglycosides it is most active against aerobic gram-negative bacteria and mycobacteria, and it synergises with cell-wall agents (penicillins) against enterococci/streptococci.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to streptomycin or other aminoglycosides
relative: Myasthenia gravis or neuromuscular disorders (neuromuscular blockade)
monitor: Baseline and periodic audiometry and vestibular function
Serum streptomycin concentrations with prolonged therapy

preg: Contraindicated. Streptomycin crosses the placenta and can cause congenital eighth-cranial-nerve damage and deafness in the infant; safer alternatives should be used.
lact: Streptomycin is excreted in breast milk in small amounts and is poorly absorbed orally by the infant; use with caution and monitor the infant.
renal: Nephrotoxic and renally eliminated - reduce the dose and/or extend the interval according to creatinine clearance and serum levels. Maintain hydration and monitor renal function closely; accumulation increases oto- and nephrotoxicity.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is needed for hepatic impairment, as elimination is renal.

major: Other ototoxic/nephrotoxic drugs (other aminoglycosides, vancomycin, amphotericin B, cisplatin, loop diuretics) - additive toxicity
Neuromuscular blocking agents and anaesthetics - enhanced neuromuscular blockade and respiratory depression
minor: Beta-lactams - synergy (therapeutically useful) but do not mix in the same syringe (inactivation)
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum creatinine; can cause electrolyte wasting (low K, Mg, Ca) with prolonged use.

serious: Ototoxicity - irreversible vestibular and/or auditory damage (hearing loss, vertigo)
emergency: Acute neuromuscular blockade with respiratory failure

monitoring: Audiometry and vestibular function at baseline and during therapy
Renal function (serum creatinine, urine output) regularly
Serum streptomycin concentrations with prolonged or high-dose therapy
Electrolytes (K, Mg, Ca) with extended use
counsel: This medicine is given by injection into the muscle as part of your treatment course
Report any ringing in the ears, hearing changes, dizziness or unsteadiness immediately
Tell your doctor about kidney problems, hearing loss or muscle-weakness conditions
Drink plenty of fluids unless told otherwise
Pregnant women must not receive this drug - tell staff if you may be pregnant
pk: Bactericidal effect rapidly after IM dose
Serum peak about 1-2 h after IM injection
Approximately 2-3 h (markedly prolonged in renal impairment)
Dosing once or twice daily; post-antibiotic effect present
Store powder at room temperature; refrigerate reconstituted solution and use within product-specified time
pearls: BOXED WARNING: neurotoxicity, ototoxicity (potentially irreversible) and nephrotoxicity - monitor hearing, balance and renal function
Contraindicated in pregnancy - causes fetal deafness
Always used in combination for tuberculosis, never as monotherapy
Adjust dose by renal function and serum levels; maintain hydration to limit nephrotoxicity
Do not mix in the same syringe as beta-lactams (mutual inactivation), though they are synergistic when co-administered
missed: Given by clinical staff; if a scheduled dose is delayed, administer as soon as practical and adjust subsequent timing to maintain the interval. Do not give a double dose to make up for a missed injection.
overdose: Overdose intensifies oto-, nephro- and neurotoxicity and may cause neuromuscular blockade with respiratory depression. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care, calcium salts/anticholinesterases for neuromuscular blockade, and haemodialysis to remove drug in severe renal failure.
